designSummary: Time-ordered weekly measurement on a run chart with pre-specified rules; p-chart as a secondary display.
sampleSize: Twenty-five comments a week is what two chief residents can rate with double rating inside their protected time. With a baseline near 26 percent, a subgroup of 25 gives 3-sigma p-chart limits of about 26 points either side of the centre line, too wide to flag single weeks, so the run chart rules carry the judgement. A sustained rise to about 45 percent would produce a shift of six or more consecutive points above the baseline median within the second cycle; the 24 intervention weeks allow the shift rule to trigger and the monthly gender breakdown to accumulate about 50 comments per group per month.
primaryAnalysis: Run chart of the weekly proportion with the baseline median as centre line; shift (six or more points on one side), trend (five or more in one direction), runs and an astronomical point agreed in advance. The median is frozen after baseline and re-estimated only after a sustained shift.
secondaryAnalysis: p-chart for context; monthly proportions by resident gender with 95 percent intervals; run charts for forms completed and days to completion; inter-rater agreement (kappa) each month.
missingData: Weeks with fewer than 25 forms are plotted with their actual subgroup size and annotated; comments that cannot be rated are counted and reported.
multiplicity: One outcome measure carries the aim; the gender breakdown and balancing measures are descriptive.
software: Spreadsheet run chart template maintained by the chief residents and checked by the associate program director.
overfittingGuards: Run chart rules fixed before baseline
Baseline median frozen until a sustained shift
Gender breakdown pre-specified; no other subgroups
Cycle changes marked on the chart before new points are read
summary: Run chart with pre-specified rules; 25 comments a week, sized by rating capacity and the change worth keeping.
